# c14 — SUYU-GURecomp facts vs. MHGU 1.4.0 disassembly

Source: SUYU-GURecomp commit 35015f1 (`nvn_trace.cpp` helper table, `arm_recomp.cpp` JIT fallback comment). Address convention: SUYU "main+X" equals our vaddr X; rows marked `sdk+` are offsets into the **nnSdk module**, because the `nvn_trace.cpp` kHelpers offsets are added to the nnSdk base, not to main (see `G:/omp works/.tmp/mhgu/suyu/sdk-helpers.txt`, which starts 8 bytes before each cited address). Our dumper prints VFP instructions as `.word ... ; coproc`; the VFP mnemonics quoted below are decoded from those encodings.

| vaddr | meaning | SUYU cite | status | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sdk+0x3f3e1c | Entry of a floating-point 64-bit helper in the nnSdk image (SUYU's `helper_double_to_int64`). It receives the 64-bit argument in r0:r1, moves it into D16 and compares it with 0.0; on a non-negative value it tail-calls the shared conversion routine at 0x455274, on a negative value it builds a real frame, negates the double, converts the magnitude, then negates the 64-bit result with `rsb`/`rsc` before returning. The `bpl` guards the only `push`, which is why a naive look at the entry finds no prologue. main+X is unrelated; this offset is sdk-relative. | nvn_trace.cpp:102 (kHelpers, added to nnSdk base) | VERIFIED | Preceding routine ends `003f3e18: e12fff1e bx lr`, so 0x3f3e1c is a fresh entry: `003f3e1c: ec410b30` (VFP `vmov d16, r0, r1`) / `003f3e20: eef50bc0` (`vcmpe.f64 d16, #0.0`) / `003f3e24: eef1fa10` (`vmrs APSR_nzcv, fpscr`) / `003f3e28: 5a000006 bpl 0x3f3e48`; the guarded arm is `003f3e2c: e92d4800 push {r11, lr}` / `003f3e30: eef10b60` (`vneg.f64 d16, d16`) / `003f3e38: eb01850d bl 0x455274` / `003f3e3c: e2700000 rsb r0, r0, #0` / `003f3e40: e2e11000 rsc r1, r1, #0` / `003f3e44: e8bd8800 pop {r11, pc}` |
| sdk+0x3f91dc | A four-byte tail-branch stub forming one entry in a run of SDK helper aliases: it forwards unchanged to 0x4501a4, sibling entries forward to 0x450ba0 and 0x450138, one of them rotating r1/r2/r3 first and another passing r1 = 0. Nothing is saved, checked or computed, which is the shape of an alias or dispatch stub for a libc-style routine such as memcpy; the four bytes themselves prove only that a distinct callable entry starts here, not which routine it aliases. main+X is unrelated; this offset is sdk-relative. | nvn_trace.cpp:103 (kHelpers, added to nnSdk base) | VERIFIED | Previous entry closes with `003f91d8: ea010773 b 0x43afac`, then the cited entry `003f91dc: ea015bf0 b 0x4501a4`, followed by `003f91e0: ea015e6e b 0x450ba0`; the next sibling `003f91e4: e1a03001 mov r3, r1` / `003f91e8: e1a01002 mov r1, r2` / `003f91ec: e1a02003 mov r2, r3` / `003f91f0: ea015bd0 b 0x450138` forwards the same target after an argument rotation |
| 0xe7ff0 | SUYU's `arm_recomp.cpp` comment names this address only as an illustration — an address that was unmapped in some crash, where the JIT fallback printed its "No recompiled ..." message. It asserts nothing about the game under analysis, so there is no SUYU fact to confirm or refute here. For the record, our main image does hold code at 0xe7ff0, so it cannot be that unmapped address; the comparison is context, not a finding. | arm_recomp.cpp:160 | SKIP | Illustrative address, not a claim: our image shows `000e7ff0: e1a0000d mov r0, sp` / `000e7ff4: eb0597bd bl 0x24def0` / `000e7ff8: e28dd018 add sp, sp, #24` / `000e7ffc: e8bd81f0 pop {r4, r5, r6, r7, r8, pc}`, with the next function starting at `000e8018: e92d4bf0 push {r4, r5, r6, r7, r8, r9, r11, lr}` after a literal run at 0xe8000-0xe8014 |
